questions.q: Why does documentation writing often get postponed on a real data team?
options: It's necessary but not urgent, and tedious to write from scratch for many columns
It is legally prohibited to document tables
Documentation cannot be written for tables with more than ten columns
Teams are never allowed to document tables without executive approval
questions.explain: This is exactly why LLM-drafted documentation is a genuinely strong use case: it removes the tedium of the first pass.

questions.q: Why does a useful documentation prompt need sample rows, not just column names?
options: Because column names alone underdetermine meaning — sample values are what actually disambiguate an ambiguous column like status
Because LLMs cannot read column names at all
Because sample rows are required by KQL syntax
Because column names are always self-explanatory and sample rows are irrelevant
questions.explain: "status" could mean an order status, shipment status, or data-quality status — sample values are what actually disambiguate it.

questions.q: What was wrong with the generated description of total_amount in this lesson's example?
options: It described total_amount as the amount charged for the order, but the cancelled row showed 0.00, meaning it reflects amount actually charged, not the original order value
It correctly described total_amount with no issues
It described total_amount as a text column when it's actually numeric
It failed to mention the column existed at all
questions.explain: The sample rows contained the evidence (a cancelled order with total_amount = 0.00) that the one-sentence draft glossed over.

questions.q: What review step catches an error like the total_amount description in this lesson?
options: Checking whether the draft description holds for every sample row shown, not just the typical-looking ones
Trusting the draft because it reads fluently
Only checking the column's data type
Skipping review since the model is usually right
questions.explain: Row 1002 (the cancelled order) breaks the draft's description — checking every sample row, including edge cases, is what catches it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson call documentation review an 'ownership' question, not just a technical one?
options: Because documentation is a claim about the business meaning of a column, which the model can't fully know without checking with whoever actually owns that meaning
Because only database administrators are allowed to write documentation
Because ownership has no bearing on whether a description is accurate
Because the model always knows the correct business meaning of every column
questions.explain: A drafted description should be checked against the person or system that actually defines what the column means in the business.
